# Livecaster

> A live co-pilot for podcast hosts. It transcribes the conversation locally while you record and,
> every ~25 seconds, asks a fast LLM to reason over your Markdown outline against the recent
> transcript. The browser UI shows the outline as a live map: covered topics strike through,
> newly relevant ones light up. At the end it writes show notes, chapters and subtitles.

This file is for agents setting Livecaster up or operating it. Humans want `README.md`.

Hard constraints, in case they decide something for you:

- The outline file is opened for reading and never for writing. The app annotates a copy.
- Audio never leaves the machine. Only outline text and transcript text reach the LLM.
- `outlines/`, `sessions/`, `.env` and `livecaster.toml` are git-ignored. They hold episode plans,
  recordings and API keys. Do not commit them, and do not paste their contents into a chat.

## Setup

Python 3.12 is pinned; `uv` is the only supported installer. Never install into a system Python.

```bash
uv sync --extra mac            # macOS on Apple Silicon: Parakeet through MLX
uv sync --extra linux          # Linux: Parakeet through onnxruntime
uv sync --extra cuda           # Linux with an NVIDIA GPU
uv sync --extra mac --extra whisper       # adds faster-whisper (forceable language, CPU, slow)
uv sync --extra mac --extra mac-whisper   # adds mlx-whisper (forceable language, GPU, pulls PyTorch)
```

The API key comes from the environment or a `.env` file in the project root:

```bash
export VENICE_API_KEY=...      # https://venice.ai, prepaid credits
```

Verify before doing anything else. This downloads ~2.4 GB of model weights on a first run:

```bash
uv run livecaster check        # key, models and prices, STT self-test, devices, permissions, disk
uv run livecaster devices      # exact device names for the config
```

If `check` reports a problem, fix it before starting a session. A failing key or a missing model
will not surface again until the host is already recording.

## Running

```bash
uv run livecaster run outlines/episode.md               # live: one room, one or more microphones
uv run livecaster run outlines/episode.md --mode remote # remote guest through the browser
uv run livecaster replay tests/fixtures/transcript_sk.jsonl --outline demo/demo.md --speed 0
uv run livecaster replay --wav sample.wav --outline demo/demo.md --mock-llm
uv run livecaster wrapup sessions/<dir>                 # re-run the show notes on a finished session
uv run livecaster export sessions/<dir>                 # re-render exports without calling the LLM
uv run livecaster run outlines/episode.md --resume sessions/<dir>
```

`--mock-llm` serves canned responses from `tests/fixtures/tick_responses/` and costs nothing. Use
it for any change you can test without the network. `--speed 0` replays as fast as the machine
allows.

Every setting can be overridden per run without touching the config file:

```bash
uv run livecaster run outlines/episode.md --set llm.tick_interval_s=15 --set stt.language=sk
LIVECASTER_LLM__TICK_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash-0731 uv run livecaster run outlines/episode.md
```

Precedence: defaults, then `livecaster.toml` (working directory, then `~/.config/livecaster/`),
then `LIVECASTER_*` environment variables, then `--set`.

## How it works

Audio path, all local. PortAudio callback enqueues frames, one segmenter thread per channel runs
Silero VAD over 32 ms frames at 16 kHz and cuts utterances on silence, and a single STT thread owns
the model because MLX and ONNX sessions are not thread-safe. Results come back to asyncio through
`loop.call_soon_threadsafe`.

Reasoning path, remote. A tick fires every `llm.tick_interval_s` once `llm.min_new_words` new words
have been said, and immediately past `llm.burst_words`. It sends the outline (byte-identical all
session, so the provider's prefix cache hits) plus a rolling window of the last
`llm.transcript_window_words` words plus the current state. The model returns candidate changes
with confidences.

The important part: **the LLM proposes and a deterministic reducer disposes.** The model never
writes state. `session/reducer.py` decides what actually happens, and its rules are not
negotiable by the model:

- a manual mark from the host always wins, and locks the model out of that item for
  `llm.manual_lock_minutes`
- a heading is covered only once its own coverable items are
- every timestamp the model returns is clamped into the transcript window it actually saw
- `covered` requires a verbatim quote from the transcript as evidence; a passing mention is
  `touched`

If you are changing behaviour, that file is where behaviour lives. Prompt changes propose;
reducer changes decide.

Persistence. `session.json` is written at most a second after any change and at least every 30 s;
the transcript, events, per-call LLM log and WAV backups stream to disk as they happen. A crash
costs the utterance in flight, and `--resume` restores the clock, the transcript and every mark.

## Models and providers

A model is written `provider:model`, or bare to use `llm.default_provider` (Venice). Venice proxies
the Claude and GPT families, so the default configuration bills one set of prepaid credits.

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `llm.tick_model` | `deepseek-v4-flash-0731-fast` | 3 to 8 s per tick, ~$0.0009 each |
| `llm.final_model` | `claude-sonnet-5` | the wrap-up, $0.14 to $0.20 per episode |
| `llm.reasoning_effort_tick` | `none` | raising it on DeepSeek V4 Flash returns empty content |
| `llm.reasoning_effort_final` | `high` | most of the wrap-up cost is the tokens it writes |

A two-hour episode costs about $0.50. To bill Anthropic or OpenAI directly, prefix the model
(`anthropic:claude-sonnet-5`) and supply that provider's key; add providers under
`[llm.providers.*]` in `livecaster.toml`.

## Speech recognition

| Engine | Language forceable | RTF | Per utterance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parakeet-mlx` (default on Apple Silicon) | no | 0.055 | ~0.25 s |
| `whisper-mlx` | yes | 0.62 | ~2.6 s |
| `faster-whisper` | yes | 3.68 | ~15 s |
| `onnx-asr` (default on Linux) | no | | |

Parakeet v3 detects the language per utterance and cannot be told which one to use. Its vocabulary
contains `<|sk|>` and the rest of the multitask token set, but neither `parakeet-mlx` nor priming
the TDT prediction network reaches them; this was measured, see `DECISIONS.md` D20. Do not add code
that pretends otherwise.

When `stt.language` is set and the engine cannot honour it, the language still fixes the prompts
and the notes, and utterances that come back in an alphabet that language never uses are dropped.
The host can also lock or release the language mid-session from the UI.

## Working on the code

```bash
uv run pytest -q                # ~400 tests, integration tests deselected by default
uv run pytest -m integration    # these call the real API and cost money
uv run ruff format . && uv run ruff check .
```

Line length is 110. Tests must pass without network access; anything that needs the API belongs
behind the `integration` marker. `DECISIONS.md` records why things are the way they are, with the
measurements behind them, and is worth reading before changing an odd-looking choice.

Layout:

```
src/livecaster/
  engine.py            orchestration: audio -> VAD -> STT -> transcript -> reasoner -> broadcast
  config.py            the whole config model; livecaster.toml mirrors it
  audio/               sources, VAD, segmenter, recorder, device enumeration
  stt/                 one Protocol, one file per engine, plus the worker thread and postprocess
  llm/                 client, provider routing, prompts, schemas, the tick loop, the wrap-up
  session/             models, the reducer, the store, transcript, exports, the fast lane
  server/              FastAPI app, WebSocket protocol, static file serving with a build id
  ui/                  vanilla JS, no build step
  templates/           Jinja2 templates for the exports
```

## When something is wrong

- LLM errors are not fatal. Transcription keeps running and ticks resume on their own with a
  5 s to 120 s backoff.
- A full STT queue means the machine cannot keep up. It drains at the end of the session.
- On macOS the microphone and system-audio permissions are granted to the terminal application,
  not to Livecaster, and some terminals never raise the prompt. BlackHole is the documented
  fallback for system audio.
- Opening a Bluetooth headset's microphone puts the link into 16 kHz handsfree mode, which
  degrades both the transcript and what the host hears. `livecaster devices` flags it.
